defects.summary: No research/ module doc is updated for the new tests, the planner arm or the seventh runtime, but the knowledge-base rule says this sync is MANDATORY; module_core's Mermaid diagram still says '18 rows (6 runtimes × 3)' and module_runners still says the kimi standing 'will be' unconfined.
MustCarryNoFlags refuses a plan with Flags or Leading but not one with AddDirs, so a hand-made plan with --add-dir is dropped silently, and decision 3 refuses a plan with ANY flag.

S5.6.5 and S5.6.6 are in a new class, not in ConfinementPlannerTests as the spec says, and this class repeats the launch builder and the KimiConsultant construction that ConfinementPlannerTests already has (Planned, Adapters).
Deviation 56 says the S5.5.3 test catches OperationCanceledException and does not assert which ending it got, but the test asserts state failed and failureKind cancelled.
The refused arm of S5.6.7 does not check the row's coai-question-* scratch.

W.summary: The production change is correct and small, and the scenario tests assert the tables' Then through the real check and the real service, with the junction recorder and the person's hash. It skips the mandatory research/ sync, does not refuse AddDirs, and puts two scenarios in a duplicated new class.

defects.summary: S5.6.7 asserts that the --cwd copy and the home folder are gone, but not that the row's coai-question-* scratch itself is gone, which the Then names.
APlanWithFlags_IsRefusedForKimi tests only Flags, so the Leading and AddDirs arms of MustCarryNoFlags have no test.
The S5.5.3 row says the check throws OperationCanceledException, but the test (correctly) asserts a recorded failed/cancelled state.
S5.5.1 asserts the canary reading 'not-attempted' as 'the canary untouched', which is a different property; the tree invariant is only implied by state answered.

X.summary: This is the most complete delivery: the correct planner arm, a flag refusal over all three plan fields, reuse of the existing Adapters() and Planned helpers, and research/ updated with the Mermaid row count and a test catalogue. It adds a useful launch-control-refusal arm to S5.6.7; the gaps are a few missing assertions and one doc line.

defects.summary: The new Kimi paragraph is added, but the Mermaid seed node still says '18 rows (6 runtimes × 3)', and module_runners still says the kimi disk standing 'will be' unconfined.
It adds a second Kimi() and PersonsPlaces builder that repeats the kimi entry Adapters() already constructs.

The refused arm compares coai-question-* folders across the whole system temp root, which is global state (the fakecli-env collection serialises it today), and the cancelled arm accepts a normal reply as well as a cancellation.
The failing arm of S5.5.2 asserts only that the state is not 'answered', and S5.5.1 does not check the <8> level of the home path.

Y.summary: Production is correct and refuses all three flag kinds, and the tests are the most honest of the four: they assert positively, through KimiHome.AfterUnlink, that a home was made, so the junction-first checks cannot pass vacuously. It loses points for duplicated test builders, a stale diagram and some loose assertions.

defects.summary: No research/ module doc is updated (tests catalogue, module_core's planner and seed diagram, module_runners), but the knowledge-base rule makes this mandatory.

It rewrites the shared 'unconfined' caveat (C# and TS) and the seed's definition of unconfined for every runtime, which is outside both stories and changes codex's user-visible text, and RuntimeCapabilities.cs still says 'a shell is always there'.
It removes the blank line between the Versions property and the next member, which breaks the file's spacing style.
S5.6.6 tests only Flags, although MustCarryNoFlag also refuses Leading and AddDirs.
S5.5.3 and S5.5.4 do not assert that the fake person's folder is intact.

Z.summary: The code and tests are correct and well reused (the Adapters kimi entry became a shared helper), with a launch-refused arm and an explicit check that the scratch is gone in S5.6.7. It skips the mandatory research/ sync and changes a shared user-facing caveat that the stories did not ask for.

reasoning: All four build the same correct planner arm, rows, vectors and generated table, and all twelve scenarios pass in each, so the decision came from refusing a plan with ANY flag, the strength of the tests, and the mandatory research/ sync. X and Y both refuse all three flag kinds and update research/; X does this more completely and with reuse, while Y has the strongest anti-vacuity assertions but duplicated builders and a stale diagram. Z and W both skip the research/ sync; Z goes above W because it covers AddDirs and checks more endings, despite its out-of-scope caveat change.
